comments.author: @ExploreTravelDocs
comments.text: Alaska has been at the top of my bucket list forever, but as someone who’s never been, I’m torn. Would you recommend experiencing the Midnight Sun in the summer first, or going all-in for the frozen winter wilderness? Which season gives you the 'real' Alaska experience?

replies.author: @DebJ77
replies.text: You’d need to decide on what’s important to you. Sleep in midnight sun season can be challenging without darkening window coverings. Polar night is the opposite. It’s always dark and headlamps & extra layers will be your reason for living. I’d go during midnight sun for your first visit, so you’re able to see your landscape. The views and wildlife will blow your mind. At the end of the day it will depend heavily on what you want to SEE. Just my 0.02 worth. I follow a girl who lives on Svalbard where they get 4 months of midnight sun and polar night. She explains in detail how to get around the fatigue and to truly enjoy your experience in either season. Cecilia Blomdahl is her name. Highly recommend her content if you want info about these stark seasons on the north.
